## Developer Guide to Toll-Free Verification | Twilio

> **Source:** https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification

# Developer Guide to Toll-Free Verification

Time to read: 7 minutes

- [Facebook logo](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification "Share via Facebook")
- [Twitter LogoFollow us on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification "Share via X")
- [LinkedIn logo](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification "Share via LinkedIn")
- [Share via Email](mailto:?subject=Developer%20Guide%20to%20Toll-Free%20Verification&body=Here%27s%20a%20link%20to%20the%20piece%20from%20Twilio:%20https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification "Share via Email")
- [Twilio RSS](https://www.twilio.com/blog.feed.xml "Twilio RSS")

October 30, 2023

**Written by**

[Twilio](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/authors/author.twilio)

Twilion


* * *

In light of the [recent announcement](https://www.twilio.com/blog/new-industry-wide-requirements-for-toll-free-messaging) that as of November 8, 2023, verification will be required for all Restricted (formerly called “Unverified”) toll-free phone numbers before they can be used for messaging, here’s a developer’s guide on toll-free registration using the [Messaging Compliance API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding).

As an alternative method of registration (via UI), you can submit your verification directly from the Twilio Console by following our [Console onboarding guide](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/console-onboarding). However, the Messaging Compliance API is better suited for handling large quantities of registrations and seamlessly integrating into existing application workflows.

## [What is happening?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#What-is-happening)

The messaging industry, along with Twilio, is continuing its shift towards a more compliant and transparent ecosystem to protect users from bad actors, spam, and unwanted communications. With [Trusted Communications](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/trust), Twilio is committed to partnering with the industry to build this trusted ecosystem so consumers are more likely to engage with legitimate messages from businesses and organizations.

Once submitted, toll-free numbers enter a Pending state and will continue having sending limits; however starting January 31, 2024, messages sent through a Pending toll-free number will be blocked and subject to messaging fees _._ The following are the current sending limits (not guaranteed maximums and are subject to change) for Pending numbers:

Daily: 2,000 message segments

Weekly: 6,000 message segments

Monthly: 10,000 message segments

[What is a Message Segment?](https://www.twilio.com/blog/what-the-heck-is-a-segment-html)

Every builder is required to comply with these requirements. Although we understand that this process introduces friction and can slow you down, it’s one of the ways we work to ensure messages are protected from spam and bad actors. Taking these steps will enable you, as developers, to continue building and innovating with messaging.

## [What number type should developers be using?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#What-number-type-should-developers-be-using)

Twilio offers a range of [phone number types](https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/223135367-Twilio-Phone-Number-Types-and-Their-Capabilities), each with its own capabilities and use cases.

[10DLC](https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/1260800720410-What-is-A2P-10DLC-), or 10-digit long codes, are standard phone numbers with messaging and voice capabilities. These numbers are great for use cases where localized, personalized communication is valued as 10DLC provides you with a local identity. These numbers offer high throughput and high delivery rates and are typically meant for individuals or businesses.

[Toll-free](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/phone-numbers/toll-free) numbers are also 10-digit phone numbers but they usually start with something like 1-833 or 1-888. They are great for universal brand identity and in the past were suited for support/sales lines but expanded their reach by supporting 2-way messaging, promotions, and notifications. Toll-free numbers are designated for medium/large business messaging and are not meant to be used for hobbyist developers.

If you are a student, hobbyist developer, or someone trying out Twilio messaging, we are exploring various solutions for you. One possibility is a Virtual Phone experience within the Twilio Console. More details will be provided closer to the launch.

If you are a business owner or ISV, you might consider 10DLC or toll-free, depending on your business needs (use case, deliverability requirements, etc).

## [I’m getting an error code (30032), what does that mean?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#Im-getting-an-error-code-30032-what-does-that-mean)

After sending a message with a toll-free number, you might get the [error code (30032): Toll-free Number has not been verified](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/30032). This could mean:

1. Your toll-free number has not been verified
2. [Your toll-free verification request was rejected](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification#rejected-verifications-or-error-codes)

To avoid this, submit your toll-free number for verification with the Messaging Compliance API, guidance in the following section.

## [I’m getting an error code (30007), what does this mean?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#Im-getting-an-error-code-30007-what-does-this-mean)

After sending a message with a toll-free number, you might get the [error code 30007](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/30007). This could mean:

1. Your toll-free phone number has been verified, but the message was filtered as spam
2. Your toll-free phone number has been submitted for verification (i.e. pending), but the message was filtered as spam

## [How do developers use the Messaging Compliance API for Toll-Free verification?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#How-do-developers-use-the-Messaging-Compliance-API-for-Toll-Free-verification)

### [Option 1: Submit a Toll-Free Verification Request without a Customer Profile](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#Option-1-Submit-a-Toll-Free-Verification-Request-without-a-Customer-Profile)

Note: If you are an ISV (Independent Software Vendor), you’ll need to [create a TrustHub primary Customer Profile](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding#prerequisites-for-isvs-create-a-trusthub-primary-customer-profile-for-your-company) for **your business** (not your customer's) and be in an APPROVED state.

Additionally, for each of your submissions, you need to provide your end-business (not your own) information as part of the submission. Toll-free verifications with ISV info will be rejected. If you set up your customers using an approved secondary Customer profile, you can then skip to [Option 2: Submit a Toll-Free Verification Request with a Customer Profile](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification#submit-toll-free-verification-request-with-customer-profile).

To create a toll-free verification record, make a POST request to the API endpoint: `[https://messaging.twilio.com/v1/Tollfree/Verifications](https://messaging.twilio.com/v1/Tollfree/Verifications)`

Code snippets will be presented in cURL, however, the Messaging Compliance API supports other [common server-side SDKs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding?code-sample=code-submit-a-toll-free-verification-request&code-language=Node.js&code-sdk-version=4.x), each accompanied by relevant code samples.

If you have not created a [Customer Profile](https://www.twilio.com/docs/trust-hub/trusthub-rest-api/customer-profiles), your request will need the [required parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding?code-sample=code-submit-a-toll-free-verification-request#option-21-a-customer-profile-sid-is-not-provided:~:text=this%20API%20endpoint.-,Request%20Parameters%3A,-Parameter) and may look like this:

Curl

Copy code

```curl
curl -X POST "https://messaging.twilio.com/v1/Tollfree/Verifications" \
# Business Address should be the business' physical location \
--data-urlencode "BusinessStreetAddress=123 Main Street" \
--data-urlencode "BusinessCity=Anytown" \
--data-urlencode "BusinessStateProvinceRegion=AA" \
--data-urlencode "BusinessPostalCode=11111" \
--data-urlencode "BusinessCountry=US" \
--data-urlencode "BusinessContactFirstName=firstname" \
--data-urlencode "BusinessContactLastName=lastname" \
--data-urlencode "BusinessContactEmail=email@company.com" \
--data-urlencode "BusinessContactPhone=+1231231234" \
# Business Name is the end business the customer is engaging with \
--data-urlencode "BusinessName=Owl, Inc." \
# Business Website is the end business website, business social media links are acceptable \
--data-urlencode "BusinessWebsite=http://www.company.com" \
--data-urlencode "NotificationEmail=support@company.com" \
# Use Case Categories cover one or more values that work best for the message traffic pattern. Make sure these match one of the allowed enums - see highlighted values. \
--data-urlencode "UseCaseCategories=ACCOUNT_NOTIFICATIONS" \
--data-urlencode "UseCaseCategories=MARKETING" \
# Use Case Summary explains how the message will be used by the business \
--data-urlencode "UseCaseSummary=This number is used to send out promotional offers and coupons to the customers of John's Coffee Shop" \
# Production Message Sample is a sample message the end business will send. It should match the Use Case Category. \
--data-urlencode "ProductionMessageSample=lorem ipsum" \
# Opt-In Image URLs should demonstrate where the end-user opts in to your message \
--data-urlencode "OptInImageUrls=https://zipwhiptestbusiness.com/images/image1.jpg" \
# Opt-In Type should outline how end users provide consent to receive messages. Make sure these match one of the allowed enums - see highlighted values. \
--data-urlencode "OptInType=VERBAL" \
# Message Volume is the estimated volume you expect \
--data-urlencode "MessageVolume=10" \
--data-urlencode "TollfreePhoneNumberSid=PNXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" \
-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN

```

Explore more and find examples of the request parameters in our detailed guide on [Toll-Free Verification request parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding?code-sample=code-submit-a-toll-free-verification-request#toll-free-verification-request-parameters).

### [Option 2: Submit a Toll-Free Verification Request with a Customer Profile](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#submit-toll-free-verification-request-with-customer-profile)

Note: If you are an ISV (Independent Software Vendor), you’ll need to [create a TrustHub primary Customer Profile](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding#prerequisites-for-isvs-create-a-trusthub-primary-customer-profile-for-your-company) for **your business** (not your customer's) and be in an APPROVED state.

Additionally, for each of your submissions, you need to provide your end-business (not your own) information as part of the submission. Toll-free verifications with ISV info will be rejected. If you set up your customers using an approved secondary Customer profile, you can then skip to [Option 2: Submit a Toll-Free Verification Request with a Customer Profile](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification#submit-toll-free-verification-request-with-customer-profile).

If you are an ISV submitting your Customer’s Profile, and you’ve already created a profile for them at Twilio, you can re-use it here.

This is best for ISVs who have created Secondary Customer Profiles at Twilio which are well-supported across products.

Your verification request will require different parameters, notably the `Customer Profile SID`.

To retrieve the `Customer Profile SID`, make a GET request like so:

Curl

Copy code

```curl
curl -X GET 'https://trusthub.twilio.com/v1/CustomerProfiles' \
-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
```

Copy the `Customer Profile SID` (String starting with _BU_), from the response, and save it for later.

Curl

Copy code

```curl
{
"sid": "BUXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
"account_sid": "ACXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
"policy_sid": "RNXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
"friendly_name": "friendly_name",

"customer_profiles_evaluations":"https://trusthub.twilio.com/v1/CustomerProfiles/BUXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX/Evaluations",
"customer_profiles_channel_endpoint_assignment":"https://trusthub.twilio.com/v1/CustomerProfiles/BUXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX/ChannelEndpointAssignments"
}

```

Using the copied `Customer Profile SID` from the previous request, make a new API request to the Verifications endpoint:

Curl

```curl
curl -X POST "https://messaging.twilio.com/v1/Tollfree/Verifications" \
# Customer Profile SID should be in an APPROVED state \
--data-urlencode "CustomerProfileSid=BUXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" \
--data-urlencode "BusinessName=Owl, Inc." \
--data-urlencode "BusinessWebsite=http://www.company.com" \

--data-urlencode "TollfreePhoneNumberSid=PNXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" \

```

### [Status of your Toll-Free Verification Request](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#Status-of-your-Toll-Free-Verification-Request)

In the request without a Customer Profile, for the response `customer_profile_sid` will be null as it’s an asynchronous process. You’ll get a webhook and an email with the `customer_profile_sid`.

In the response, you’ll see a `status` for your verification. To monitor this status, make a GET request with the Toll-Free number used for verification:

Curl

Copy code

```curl
curl -X GET 'https://messaging.twilio.com/v1/Tollfree/Verifications?TollfreePhoneNumberSid=PNXXXXXXXXX' \
-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN

```

Here’s an overview of each verification status from the API:

| **Verification Status** | **Toll-Free Phone Number Traffic** | **Traffic Limits** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PENDING\_REVIEW | Restricted | Starting on November 8, 2023, ALL Restricted traffic will be blocked. |
| IN\_REVIEW | Pending Verification | Sending Limits (not guaranteed)**Daily: 2,000 message segments**Weekly: 6,000 message segments**Monthly: 10,000 message segments. |
| TWILIO\_APPROVED | Approved | 3 SMS segments per second by default, but can be increased. |
| TWILIO\_REJECTED | If re-submittable, Pending.**If not re-submittable, Blocked.**If after the 7-day resubmission response window, Restricted | Blocked. |

Additionally, you can list all Toll-Free verification records and view their status by making a GET request to the Verifications endpoint with an optional `PageSize` parameter:

Curl

Copy code

```curl
curl -X GET "https://messaging.twilio.com/v1/Tollfree/Verifications?PageSize=20" \
-u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN

```

In addition to making requests for monitoring the verification status, you can [receive status updates through emails](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding?code-sample=code-submit-a-toll-free-verification-request&code-language=Node.js&code-sdk-version=4.x#email-notification) or get [notified via webhooks](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding?code-sample=code-submit-a-toll-free-verification-request&code-language=Node.js&code-sdk-version=4.x#webhooks) through Event Streams.

## [Rejected Verifications or Error Codes](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#rejected-verifications-or-error-codes)

If your Toll-Free verification request has been rejected, you can edit and re-submit the verification depending on the returned [error code](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding?code-sample=code-submit-a-toll-free-verification-request&code-language=Node.js&code-sdk-version=4.x#rejected-verifications). _It's best to edit and resubmit within 7 days._

Alternatively, you can [delete the verification submission](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/console-onboarding#5-delete-a-toll-free-verification) in the Twilio Console.

## [The Future of Trusted Communications](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developer-guide-to-toll-free-verification\#The-Future-of-Trusted-Communications)

This November 8, 2023 date when all messages sent from Restricted (or “Unverified”) toll-free phone numbers will be blocked is the next step towards a fully verified and trusted messaging ecosystem. As the messaging and communications ecosystem continues to change around the world, Twilio is dedicated to creating a trusted and compliant ecosystem for our customers.

For additional information, please reference our Docs on [Toll-Free Verification API Onboarding](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/compliance/toll-free/api-onboarding).

# Build Real-Time Voice Translation with Python, FastAPI, and Twilio ConversationRelay

Time to read: 4 minutes

- [Facebook logo](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay "Share via Facebook")

* * *

[Build Real-Time Voice Translation with Python, FastAPI, and Twilio ConversationRelay](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay#introduction)

Language barriers in real-time communication have always presented a fascinating technical challenge: _How do you build a system that can seamlessly translate conversations between two people speaking different languages during a live phone call?_

A previous serverless [demo](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/translation-with-conversationrelay) tackled this using AWS’s infrastructure, but this new project takes a different approach with FastAPI and Python. Using Twilio's [ConversationRelay](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/connect/conversationrelay), [OpenAI](https://openai.com/)'s translation capabilities, and modern web technologies, this demo explores how real-time, cross-lingual communication can be made efficient and scalable.

This demo project tackles these challenges using a modern tech stack to create a working proof-of-concept.

## [Demo app overview](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay\#demo-app-overview)

This demo app enables real-time, bidirectional voice translation between two phone participants. Each person can speak and hear in their own language. The system is built on a scalable [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend and uses Twilio ConversationRelay to manage calls and media processing.

**Key Features**

- **Bidirectional Translation**: Both parties can speak and hear in their preferred languages.
- **Configurable Languages**: Set phone numbers, source and target languages through Web UI.
- **Scalable Architecture**: Uses FastAPI and asynchronous processing for high performance.

## [Technical architecture](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay\#technical-architecture)

![Diagram showing Twilio call flow through ConvRelay and WebSocket to a server, ending in stream mode to OpenAI.](https://www.twilio.com/content/dam/twilio-com/global/en/blog/importer-images/p-s/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay/media1/_jcr_content/renditions/compressed-original.webp)

![](https://www.twilio.com/content/dam/twilio-com/global/en/blog/importer-images/p-s/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay/media1/_jcr_content/renditions/compressed-original.webp)

### [Core components in the application](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay\#core-components-in-the-application)

To better understand how this application works under the hood, here’s a breakdown of the key components and endpoints that power real-time voice translation. These elements coordinate call sessions, handle WebSocket communication, process voice input, and manage translation flows—working together to deliver a seamless multilingual conversation experience.

- Translation Session Management
- `TranslationSession` class manages call pairs and WebSocket connections
- Tracks source and target call SIDs, phone numbers, and languages
- Maintains WebSocket connections for both callers
- WebSocket Endpoints
- `/ws/source/{session_id}` \- Handles source caller WebSocket
- `/ws/target/{session_id}` \- Handles target callee WebSocket
- Real-time bidirectional voice processing
- Voice Webhooks
- `/voice/source/{session_id}` \- Outbound call webhook for source language speaker
- `/voice/target/{session_id}` \- Outbound call webhook for target language speaker
- Translation Engine
-  Streaming translation using [LiteLLM](https://www.litellm.ai/) and OpenAI GPT-4
- Configurable source and target languages

### [How it works](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay\#how-it-works)

The system creates a bridge between caller and callee through the following flow:

1. **Session Management:** Each translation session initiates two outbound calls—one to the source (caller) and one to the target (callee).
2. **ConvRelay Configuration:** Outbound call webhooks are configured to set up ConversationRelay sockets for media streaming.
3. **Bi-Directional flow:**
- On the source-to-target path:
- ConvRelay Socket 1 receives transcribed text from the Source Caller (via internal STT).
- The text is translated and sent to ConvRelay Socket 2, where it is converted back to speech (via TTS) and played to the Target Callee.
- On the target-to-source path:
- ConvRelay Socket 2 captures the Target Callee's speech, transcribes it to text (via internal STT), and sends it to ConvRelay Socket 1.
- The text is translated and synthesized (via TTS) before being played to the Source Caller.

## [Get started with the demo](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay\#get-started-with-the-demo)

### [Prerequisites](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay\#prerequisites)

- Python 3.8+
- [UV](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) for python package management
- API keys for the LLM providers you’d like to test (OpenAI is used In this demo)
- [ngrok](https://ngrok.com/) for exposing your test server to Twilio
- A Twilio account and a [registered phone number with voice capabilities](https://help.twilio.com/articles/223135247-How-to-Search-for-and-Buy-a-Twilio-Phone-Number-from-Console)

### [Run the demo locally](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay\#run-the-demo-locally)

Now I’ll walk you through cloning the repo, getting everything set up, then running and calling the translation app.

1\. Clone the Git repository:

Bash

Copy code

```bash
git clone https://github.com/midshipman/ConversationRelay-Translate
cd conversationrelay-translate
```

2\. Install Dependencies with: uv sync

3\. Configure Environment Variables: Copy .env.sample to .env ( \`cp .env.sample .env\` and add your Twilio and OpenAI credentials in your favorite text editor or IDE. Also add a Twilio number where the call will be made from, in [E.164 format.](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164) You can find your Twilio credentials [here in your Twilio Console](https://console.twilio.com/).

4\. Run the application:

Bash

Copy code

```bash
uv run main.py
```

5\. Run Ngrok: Expose the application on the internet from your local machine.

Bash

Copy code

```bash
ngrok http 8080
```

6\. Access the demo app by using the link provided by Ngrok in step 5.

## [Test the demo](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay\#test-the-demo)

Ready to see the magic in action? You’ll need two phone numbers—one for each participant. Think of it like setting up a cross-language conversation between two people who don't speak the same language!

Choose a language for each person, and the system will automatically place two outbound calls using your Twilio number (configured in your _.env_ file). You can also select your favorite [ElevenLabs](https://elevenlabs.io/) voice to personalize the experience even further, use this [document](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/conversationrelay/voice-configuration#elevenlabs-voices) to start. Once connected, you’ll hear real-time translation kick in – _just_ like having a personal interpreter on the line.

It’s a great way to experience what you’ve just built, and it feels pretty cool seeing it all come together!

![Screenshot of translation call settings with details for two participants including language and TTS provider.](https://www.twilio.com/content/dam/twilio-com/global/en/blog/importer-images/p-s/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay/media2/_jcr_content/renditions/compressed-original.webp)

![](https://www.twilio.com/content/dam/twilio-com/global/en/blog/importer-images/p-s/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay/media2/_jcr_content/renditions/compressed-original.webp)

## [Conclusion](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/real-time-voice-translation-python-fastapi-conversationrelay\#conclusion)

This demo showcases how you can use FastAPI, Python, Twilio’s ConversationRelay, and large language models (LLMs) together to address complex real-time communication challenges. While there's still work to be done to make it production-ready, this foundation highlights the powerful potential of using technology to break down language barriers.

## AI & Twilio for Smarter Medication Reminders | Twilio

> **Source:** https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/automated-medication-reminders-ai

# Automated Medication Reminders: AI & Twilio for Better Adherence

Time to read: 5 minutes

- [Facebook logo](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/automated-medication-reminders-ai "Share via Facebook")
- [Twitter LogoFollow us on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/automated-medication-reminders-ai "Share via X")

- [Share via Email](mailto:?subject=Automated%20Medication%20Reminders%20|%20AI%20&%20Twilio%20for%20Better%20Adherence&body=Here%27s%20a%20link%20to%20the%20piece%20from%20Twilio:%20https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/automated-medication-reminders-ai "Share via Email")
- [Twilio RSS](https://www.twilio.com/blog.feed.xml "Twilio RSS")

March 19, 2025

**Written by**

[Kike Rodriguez](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/authors/author.kike-rodriguez)

Twilion


**Reviewed by**

[Hana Hassan](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/authors/author.hhassan)

Twilion


* * *

In elderly care, one of the most common challenges is ensuring that they take their medications in a timely and accurate manner. Forgetfulness or confusion about dosages can have serious consequences, especially for individuals who must follow complex regimens to treat multiple conditions. Today, Twilio’s technology, combined with artificial intelligence, could offer a revolutionary solution: an automated system that, based on an analysis of the medical history, schedules and sends daily reminders via SMS, WhatsApp, or push notifications can help to improve adherence and, consequently, the wellbeing of our elderly.

## The Solution: Automated Medication Reminder

With the technological advances we have achieved today in data analysis and communication channels, we can envision various solutions to help solve the medication adherence problem for the elderly. Imagine developing an intelligent platform that performs the following functions:

- **Scanning the Medical History:** All medical centers maintain records for each of their patients. These records include relevant information such as age, ailments and diseases, and the medication that is supplied or should be supplied. Medical criteria dictate that medication always depends on different variables like age, condition, and type of medication. Therefore, some medications must be supplied daily, others every two days, and some more than once a day. In designing this solution, AI analyzes the patient’s medical history to identify the prescribed medications, their dosages, and the specific times for administration—all based on medical criteria that allow for a controlled and appropriate assignment of medication according to each patient’s needs.
- **Scheduling Reminders:** With the information gathered from scanning the medical history, different user profiles can be created. Based on this information, automatic reminders are set up and sent to mobile devices via SMS, WhatsApp, or push notifications. The channel can be chosen by each user or according to the preferences registered in their profile.
- **Dose Confirmation:** It is important to emphasize that the goal of this implementation is to have a positive impact on elderly care. Therefore, a crucial step to ensure the desired impact on the patient is to confirm both the receipt of the message and the subsequent confirmation that the medication has been taken correctly by the patient. Accordingly, the system requests a confirmation from the patient or their caregiver, allowing for adherence monitoring. This confirmation is then recorded in the patient’s profile in the database to maintain clear control over the notification and the correct consumption of the medication.
- **Alerts for Caregivers:** As established in this document, the main objective of this solution is the wellbeing of the elderly who are taking the medications. Therefore, functionalities must be implemented that, in case the patient does not confirm taking the medication, trigger an alert to family members or caregivers so that they can intervene promptly. Again, this notification to family members and caregivers will include a confirmation option to help maintain control over the patient’s medical history.

This solution not only focuses on reminding patients about their medication, but it also offers continuous and personalized follow-up, which can make a significant difference in the quality of life and health of elderly people.

![Diagram showing an automated customer response workflow with AI, data, and messaging integration.](https://www.twilio.com/content/dam/twilio-com/global/en/blog/insights/digital-insights-imagery-by-post/a-c/medication-reminders-flow-chart.png/_jcr_content/renditions/compressed-original.webp)

![Diagram showing an automated customer response workflow with AI, data, and messaging integration.](https://www.twilio.com/content/dam/twilio-com/global/en/blog/insights/digital-insights-imagery-by-post/a-c/medication-reminders-flow-chart.png/_jcr_content/renditions/compressed-original.webp)

**Automated Customer Response Workflow with AI, Data, and Messaging Integration**

## Implementation Strategies

To successfully deploy this solution, it is crucial to follow a series of implementation strategies:

**Integration with Electronic Medical Records:**

- **Data Extraction:** Use AI algorithms to extract relevant data from each patient’s digital medical history, such as the name of the medication, dosage, and schedules.
- **Security and Privacy:** Ensure that all data is managed under strict security protocols and complies with data protection regulations, such as HIPAA or GDPR.

**Use of Twilio’s APIs and Solutions**

- **Multichannel Messaging:** Utilize Twilio’s SMS, WhatsApp, and push notification APIs to send reminders on the channel preferred by the user.
- **Twilio Segment:** Employ solutions like Twilio Segment to centralize the data of each user profile and maintain control over the medication supply, which can then be analyzed and processed directly by AI.
- **Functions:** Develop functions that can identify when a user receives and responds to a medication reminder in a timely manner; if not, trigger a new notification to their caregiver, family member, or nurse in charge.
- **Workflow Automation:** Configure automated communication flows that, upon detecting the medication time, activate the timely sending of reminders.

**Personalization Through AI:**

- **Predictive Analysis:** Use machine learning models to predict adherence patterns and dynamically adjust the reminders according to the patient’s behavior. Reviewing the medical history is key, as medical diagnoses may suggest changes in medication that will affect the reminders or require dosage adjustments, which must be considered to vary the periodicity of the reminder notifications.

**User-Friendly and Accessible Interface:**

- **Intuitive Design:** Develop a simple mobile application so that both the elderly and their caregivers can configure, view, and manage the reminders.
- **Multilingual Support:** Ensure that the solution supports multiple languages, facilitating its use in different regions and adapting to the needs of a diverse population.

## Projected Benefits

The development of a solution focused on the elderly aims to improve quality of life and patient interaction by providing technological tools that make the medication process more efficient through the use of advanced Twilio and AI technologies. Some of the most notable benefits include:

- **Improved Adherence:**


Personalized reminders help ensure that patients do not forget their medications, reducing complications and hospitalizations.
- **Peace of Mind for Families:**


Confirmation of medication intake and automatic alerts allow caregivers to stay informed and act quickly in case of any omission.
- **Optimization of Medical Resources:** By reducing the time spent on calls and manual follow-up, healthcare professionals can focus on more critical cases.
- **Continuous Personalization:** AI learns and adapts to individual needs, allowing adjustments to the frequency and content of reminders based on patient behavior.

## Conclusion

Elderly wellbeing can be significantly enhanced through the integration of emerging technologies. The combination of the robustness and flexibility of Twilio’s communication APIs with the predictive and customizable capabilities of artificial intelligence enables the automation of the medication reminder process. This solution not only improves adherence to treatment but also provides greater peace of mind for caregivers and optimizes healthcare resources.

If you are looking to transform the way your patients receive their medication reminders and ensure more rigorous follow-up, now is the time to explore the possibilities offered by Twilio and AI.

Are you ready to innovate in elderly care and improve their quality of life? Technology is here to help you achieve it!

## What is speech recognition and how does it work? | Twilio

> **Source:** https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition

# What is speech recognition and how does it work?

Time to read: 5 minutes

[What is speech recognition and how does it work?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition#introduction)

The human voice is a powerful tool for conveying thoughts, emotions, and ideas. While speech has historically been a human trait distinct from machines, the landscape is shifting. Traditionally, our interactions with computers were limited to devices like keyboards and consoles. However, today's advancements in speech recognition software have revolutionized this interaction, enabling seamless communication between people and technology.

Speech recognition technology can be a game-changer for businesses. It can help streamline operations and improve customer experiences with ease. For example, imagine a customer support system that instantly understands and processes customer inquiries without the need for typing. Or an automatic transcription of meetings that can be distributed to everyone who couldn’t attend. Or real-time translations. There are many possibilities, which we’ll discuss below.

In short, speech recognition technology equips businesses with tools to operate more efficiently and engage more effectively, turning spoken words into actionable insights.

## [What is speech recognition technology?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#toc-heading-38e0a2bc-abcc-4980-9bc3-3dd560fdb076)

Speech recognition is the technology that enables computers and devices to understand and process human speech. It involves converting spoken language into text or commands that a computer can understand and act upon. This technology captures audio input, analyzes the sounds, and matches them to words or phrases in its database to produce an accurate interpretation.

Speech recognition is used in various applications, such as virtual assistants (like [Siri](https://www.apple.com/siri/), [Alexa](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DCCNHWV5?ref=aucc_web_red_xaa_evgn_tx_0002), or [Google Assistant](https://assistant.google.com/)), customer service bots, transcription services, and more. Its ability to facilitate hands-free interaction with technology not only enhances user convenience but also makes tech more accessible to individuals with physical limitations or those in environments where using hands isn't feasible.

## [How does speech recognition work?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#toc-heading-f5cc6879-b97c-40cd-b741-5959c7fe171f)

Speech recognition technologies capture the human voice with physical devices like receivers or microphones. The hardware digitizes recorded sound vibrations into electrical signals. Then, the software attempts to identify sounds and phonemes—the smallest unit of speech—from the signals and match these sounds to corresponding text. Depending on the application, this text displays on the screen or triggers a directive—like when you ask your smart speaker to play a specific song and it does.

Background noise, accents, slang, and cross talk can interfere with speech recognition, but advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning technologies filter through these anomalies to increase precision and performance.

Thanks to new and emerging machine learning algorithms, speech recognition offers advanced capabilities:

- [Natural language processing](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-natural-language-processing-nlp) is a branch of computer science that uses AI to emulate how humans engage in and understand speech and text-based interactions.

- Hidden Markov Models (HMM) are statistical models that assign text labels to units of speech—like words, syllables, and sentences—in a sequence. Labels map to the provided input to determine the correct label or text sequence.

- N-grams are language models that assign probabilities to sentences or phrases to improve speech recognition accuracy. These contain sequences of words and use prior sequences of the same words to understand or predict new words and phrases. These calculations improve the predictions of sentence automatic completion systems, spell-check results, and even grammar checks.

- Neural networks consist of node layers that together emulate the learning and decision-making capabilities of the human brain. Nodes contain inputs, weights, a threshold, and an output value. Outputs that exceed the threshold activate the corresponding node and pass data to the next layer. This means remembering earlier words to continually improve recognition accuracy.

- Connectionist temporal classification is a neural network algorithm that uses probability to map text transcript labels to incoming audio. It helps train neural networks to understand speech and build out node networks.


## [Speech recognition features to look for](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#5-speech-recognition-features-to-look-for)

Not all speech recognition works the same. Implementations vary by application, but each uses AI to quickly process speech at a high—but not flawless—quality level. Many speech recognition technologies include the same features:

1. Filtering identifies and censors—or removes—specified words or phrases to sanitize text outputs.

2. Language weighting assigns more value to frequently spoken words—like proper nouns or industry jargon—to improve speech recognition precision.

3. Speaker labeling distinguishes between multiple conversing speakers by identifying contributions based on vocal characteristics.

4. Acoustics training analyzes conditions—like ambient noise and particular speaker styles—then tailors the speech recognition software to that environment. It’s useful when recording speech in busy locations, like call centers and offices.

5. [Voice recognition](https://www.twilio.com/blog/what-is-voice-recognition) helps speech recognition software pivot the listening approach to each user’s accent, dialect, and grammatical library.


## [5 benefits of speech recognition technology](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#5-benefits-of-speech-recognition-technology)

The popularity and convenience of speech recognition technology have made speech recognition a big part of everyday life. Adoption of this technology will only continue to spread, so learn more about how speech recognition transforms how we live and work:

1. **Speed:** Speaking with your voice is faster than typing with your fingers—in most cases.

2. **Assistance:** Listening to directions from users and taking action accordingly is possible thanks to speech recognition technology. For instance, if your vehicle’s sound system has speech recognition capabilities, you can tell it to tune the radio to a particular channel or map directions to a specified address.

3. **Productivity**: Dictating your thoughts and ideas instead of typing them out, saves time and effort to redirect toward other tasks. To illustrate, picture yourself dictating a report into your smartphone while walking or driving to your next meeting.

4. **Intelligence:** Learning from and adapting to your unique speech habits and environment to identify and understand you better over time is possible thanks to speech recognition applications.

5. **Accessibility:** Entering text with speech recognition is possible for people with visual impairments who can’t see a keyboard thanks to this technology. Software and websites like Google Meet and YouTube can accommodate hearing-impaired viewers with text captions of live speech translated to the user’s specific language.


## [7 speech recognition use cases for businesses](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/ai/what-is-speech-recognition\#7-speech-recognition-use-cases-for-businesses)

Speech recognition directly connects products and services to customers. It powers interactive voice recognition software that delivers customers to the right support agents—each more productive with faster, hands-free communication. Along the way, speech recognition captures actionable insights from customer conversations you can use to bolster your organization’s operational and marketing processes.

Here are some real-world speech recognition contexts and applications:

1. **SMS/MMS messages:** Write and send SMS or MMS messages conveniently in some environments.

2. **Chatbot discussions:** Get answers to product or service-related questions any time of day or night with chatbots.

3. **[Web browsing](https://www.twilio.com/blog/speech-recognition-browser-web-speech-api):** Browse the internet without a mouse, keyboard, or touch screen through voice commands.

4. **Active learning:** Enable students to enjoy interactive learning applications—such as those that teach a new language—while teachers create lesson plans.

5. **Document writing:** Draft a Google or Word document when you can't access a physical or digital keyboard with speech-to-text. You can later return to the document and refine it once you have an opportunity to use a keyboard. Doctors and nurses often use these applications to log patient diagnoses and treatment notes efficiently.

6. **Phone transcriptions:** Help callers and receivers transcribe a conversation between 2 or more speakers with [phone APIs](https://www.twilio.com/blog/transcribe-phone-calls-text-real-time-twilio-vosk).

7. **Interviews:** Turn spoken words into a comprehensive speech log the interviewer can reference later with this software. When a journalist interviews so

## Abandoned cart recovery strategies for marketers | Twilio

# 12 abandoned cart recovery strategies for marketers

[12 abandoned cart recovery strategies for marketers](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies#introduction)

If you don't know how to reduce cart abandonment, you could be leaving money on the table. According to a Baymard Institute analysis, [the average ecommerce company loses 70.19% of checkouts to shopping cart abandonment](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate). Many of these losses can be recovered by implementing a proactive abandoned cart strategy. Baymard estimates that companies taking steps to improve checkout processes can enjoy a 35.26% increase in conversion rates, while US and EU companies could recover $260 billion annually by prioritizing abandoned cart recovery.

In this blog, we'll show you how to improve cart abandonment rates. We'll explain what abandoned cart recovery is, examine why customers abandon their carts, and discuss how to calculate cart abandonment rate and evaluate cart performance. Then, we'll share 12 abandoned cart best practices to help you convert abandoned carts into successful purchases.

## [What is abandoned cart recovery?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#what-is-abandoned-cart-recovery)

To lay a foundation, let's start by answering the basic question: what is cart abandonment recovery? Online shopping cart abandonment occurs whenever a customer initiates a digital checkout but fails to complete the process. Abandoned cart recovery is a proactive strategy for preventing abandonment incidents and intervening when they occur to promote checkout completion.

Abandoned cart recovery strategies consist of steps to reduce abandonment at every stage of the checkout process. These include steps for:

- Preventing abandonment before the checkout process

- Catching abandonment during checkouts

- Responding after abandonment occurs


Strategies for reducing abandonment include improving checkout usability, offering various shipping options, and sending emails and texts to encourage checkout completion. Cart abandonment solutions support these strategies by enabling companies to send [abandoned cart emails](https://www.twilio.com/docs/labs/firebase-extensions/abandoned-cart-emails) and texts and track checkout performance.

Ecommerce companies prioritize abandoned cart recovery because it represents one of the most efficient ways to increase sales. Customers who abandon their carts are already leaning toward making a purchase, making them more likely to buy from you than prospects who haven't even started the checkout process.

You have to invest considerably more time and effort into acquiring new leads and persuading them to buy than you would in salvaging abandoned sales. Making the extra effort to win over customers who abandon their carts can be one of the least costly marketing strategies to generate more revenue.

## [Why do customers abandon their carts?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#why-do-customers-abandon-their-carts)

Baymard research (linked above) has identified the top 10 reasons for online shopping cart abandonment. Factoring out window shoppers who were just browsing, the most common reasons customers cited for abandoning their carts were:

01. High extra costs, such as shipping, fees, and taxes (48%)

02. Account creation requirements (26%)

03. Credit card security concerns (25%)

04. Slow delivery times (23%)

05. Long checkout processes (22%)

06. No up-front total calculation (21%)

07. Unsatisfactory return policies (18%)

08. Website errors (17%)

09. Limited payment options (13%)

10. Declined credit cards (9%)


As these results indicate, customers typically abandon carts due to cost, convenience, security, or shipping concerns. Abandoned cart recovery strategies focus on mitigating these issues.

## [How do I calculate cart abandonment rate?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#how-do-i-calculate-cart-abandonment-rate)

Shopping cart abandonment rate can be calculated over a given time frame by applying the formula:

    CAR = \[1 – (CC/TC)\] \* 100

Where:

CAR = cart abandonment rate

CC = completed carts

TC = total carts

To illustrate, let's say that over a month, customers opened 1,000 carts and completed 250 purchases:

    CAR = \[1 – (250/1,000)\] \*100 = 75%

In this example, your cart abandonment rate for the month would be 75%.

When interpreting shopping cart abandonment rates, marketing teams should consider them in the context of other factors. For example, the quality and volume of visits can affect rates if your site is attracting window shoppers. Likewise, technical problems with your site or checkout process can increase abandonment rates. To put the cart abandonment rate in context, consider other important key performance indicators (KPIs) such as site speed and conversion rate.

## [What is a good abandoned cart recovery rate?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#what-is-a-good-abandoned-cart-recovery-rate)

Baymard's research indicates that cart abandonment rates average 70.19%. This means that, on average, recovering more than 29.81% of abandoned carts reflects an improvement. The average large ecommerce site can increase recovery rates by 35.26% by improving checkout process usability.

Average rates vary by industry, company, and product. For perspective, monitor and benchmark your internal numbers and research competitors' performance.

## [How to reduce cart abandonment](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#how-to-reduce-cart-abandonment)

Strategies for reducing cart abandonment address common reasons customers abandon carts. Cart abandonment solutions help implement these strategies by streamlining checkout processes, monitoring performance, and supporting recovery emails and texts. Let's look at how to put these strategies into effect.

### [1\. Show clear calls to action (CTAs).](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#1-show-clear-calls-to-action-ctas)

CTAs can guide customers through the checkout process. This reduces the risk of shoppers abandoning carts over confusion about how to proceed. Use CTAs to:

- Help customers add items

- Initiate checkouts

- Enter shipping and billing information

- Choose shipping options

- Select payment methods

- Complete transactions


### [2\. Display shipping options on your product pages.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#2-display-shipping-options-on-your-product-pages)

If customers know their shipping options before they initiate checkout, they're less likely to abandon carts over shipping issues. Allow them to select their shipping location on product pages so they can see the available shipping options.

### [3\. Give customers a guest checkout option.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#3-give-customers-a-guest-checkout-option)

Requiring customers to create an account before checking out adds an extra step that can dissuade them from completing transactions. Even customers with accounts may hesitate to check out if they need to spend additional time retrieving credentials and completing login procedures. Simplify your checkout process by allowing customers to check out as guests without logging in.

### [4\. Be transparent about total costs.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#4-be-transparent-about-total-costs)

Fees that exceed expectations prompt more customers to abandon carts than any other factor. Avoid sticker shock by being up front about total costs. List itemized costs early in the checkout process so customers can see what they're paying for and choose less expensive options before abandoning orders.

### [5\. Include a thumbnail of cart contents.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#5-include-a-thumbnail-of-cart-contents)

Shopping cart thumbnail icons help customers see what's in their cart and what it costs while also enabling them to remove or add items. This reduces the risk of customers abandoning carts due to price concerns or unwanted items. Increase conversions by including a highly visible cart thumbnail image at the top of your customer's user interface.

### [6\. Use analytics to monitor cart abandonment.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#6-use-analytics-to-monitor-abandonment)

Analytics tools let you track abandonment activity using KPIs and reports. This enables you to see how often customers are abandoning carts and identify trends that may indicate the reasons for cart abandonment. Ecommerce platforms and shopping cart software typically include these analytics tools.

### [7\. Include progress indicators on the checkout page.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#7-include-progress-indicators-on-the-checkout-page)

Progress indicators reassure customers that they're taking the correct steps to complete their purchase, which decreases cart abandonment stemming from confusion about the checkout process. Break your checkout process down into clear steps, such as selecting items, entering addresses, choosing shipping methods, and selecting payment methods. Use indicators to show customers which steps have been completed and which actions still need to be taken.

### [8\. Utilize exit intent pop-ups.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#8-utilize-exit-intent-popups)

Exit intent pop-ups are overlays that appear when customers are about to abandon their carts, giving them a second chance to reconsider completing their purchase. Increase the likelihood of conversion by offering incentives like discounts or special offers for finishing their order.

### [9\. Save cart contents.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#9-save-cart-contents)

Customers who abandon cart items may have been interrupted by technical problems, distractions at home, or temporary financial issues. In such scenarios, they may be inclined to order the items later when they resume shopping. Give them the opportunity to pick up where they left off by saving the contents of abandoned carts.

### [10\. Offer several payment options.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#10-offer-several-payment-options)

Customers may abandon carts if their preferred payment option isn't available. Accommodate them by offering multiple payment options. This can include allowing customers to add multiple credit cards to their account so they can choose which one to use.

### [11\. Create a comprehensive return policy.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#11-create-a-comprehensive-return-policy)

Customers may abandon carts if they're concerned about refunds for returned items. Remove this barrier by creating a clear return policy, posting it prominently, and making it easily accessible. Include links to your return policy in page footers, on product pages, and within checkout carts.

### [12\. Send cart recovery emails and texts.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#12-send-cart-recovery-emails-and-texts)

Apart from window shoppers, most customers who abandon carts initially had an interest in making a purchase. This presents an opportunity to rekindle their interest by reaching out with email and text offers. Cart abandonment solutions support this strategy by providing tools for automatically sending personalized messages to customers who abandon carts.

To assist you with sending recovery messages, Twilio offers tools for texting and emailing customers, along with [text message examples](https://www.twilio.com/blog/promotional-text-message-examples) and [abandoned cart email templates](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/free-templates/detail/abandoned-cart-email-template/download?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fbest-practices%2Fabandoned-cart-recovery-strategies) that you can adapt to your needs.

## [Reduce cart abandonment and re-engage customers](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/abandoned-cart-recovery-strategies\#reduce-cart-abandonment-and-reengage-customers) with Twilio

Cart abandonment doesn't have to cut into conversions if you apply the recovery strategies recommended in this article. Successful implementation of these strategies depends on using the right tools.

[Twilio's text marketing solutions](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/solutions/text-marketing) support cart abandonment recovery by enabling you to reengage shoppers with SMS texts. Recapture conversion opportunities with automated, personalized messages. ## Organizational Silos in Business: Pros, Cons &, Fix | Twilio

> **Source:** https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos

# Organizational Silos: Causes, Cons, and How to Break Down Departmental Walls

Time to read: 6 minutes

- [Facebook logo](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos "Share via Facebook")
- [Twitter LogoFollow us on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos "Share via X")

- [Share via Email](mailto:?subject=Organizational%20Silos%20in%20Business:%20Pros,%20Cons,%20&%20How%20to%20Fix&body=Here%27s%20a%20link%20to%20the%20piece%20from%20Twilio:%20https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos "Share via Email")

June 08, 2023

**Written by**

[Twilio Segment](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/authors/author.twilio-segment)

Contributor


Opinions expressed by Twilio contributors are their own

* * *

[Organizational Silos: Causes, Cons, and How to Break Down Departmental Walls](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos#introduction)

Say a marketing team at a startup SaaS company has been working around the clock to prepare for an upcoming product launch. But just days before their launch date, they learn the product will lack several important functionalities and features they had planned on. Now, they have to rework their entire strategy with just a few days at their disposal.

This is an example of how organizational silos can create a breakdown of communication.

If left unchecked, silos erode employee and customer satisfaction, stifle growth, and create chaos in your data systems.

## [What are organizational silos?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos\#toc-heading-bbc6b5b8-f985-48d7-abe4-0c9b3f21b97d)

Organizational silos occur when employees work in isolation according to their department, physical location, rank, or schedule. In extreme cases, organizational silos lead to a silo mentality, where different departments purposefully don’t want to share information with each other.

In silos, there is very little cross-team collaboration, which leads to inefficient communication, confusion, and delays.

## [4 causes of organizational silos](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos\#4-causes-of-organizational-silos)

The causes of organizational silos are multifold, ranging from poor management to turf wars between departments.

### **1\. Poor leadership**

When leadership fails to communicate their vision for the business with the entire organization, they lay the groundwork for departmental silos. Individual teams become hyper focused on their own goals, rather than how those goals fit within the overarching business strategy.

### **2\. Isolated departments**

Without effective collaboration across teams, departments work in isolation, unaware of how their efforts impact other teams. For instance, customer support may be sitting on a wealth of valuable feedback from users, but they haven’t shared it with the product team (meaning insights on product usability aren’t being factored into the roadmap).

### **3\. Hybrid work cultures**

Hybrid workplaces can also be prone to silos based on location. It can be difficult to forge connections within a widespread, remote workspace, and it can be easy to forget to include people (e.g., teammates in the office don’t invite remote colleagues to dial in to an impromptu brainstorm session).

### **4\. Competition and favoritism**

Favoritism manifests itself as limiting information-sharing to a select group of employees, or awarding one department a bigger budget for ambiguous reasons. A company culture that tolerates unhealthy competition results in silos as employees and managers seek to outperform others rather than work together.

## [Why organizational silos are problematic](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos\#why-organizational-silos-are-problematic)

A siloed organizational structure creates challenges on multiple levels, both for the customer and for internal teams.

### **1\. Unable to access important data**

Organizational silos lead to data silos. Teams store information in separate applications, causing departments to work off different data sets. In an extremely siloed culture, departments might not be willing to share data with other teams, which also means data is incomplete.

Poor data quality is an expensive issue to have. According to IBM estimates, the annual cost of poor-quality data is $3.1 trillion.

### **2\. Cross-department rivalry**

When departmental silos form, teams focus on achieving their own goals rather than those of the company. Instead of seeing other departments as different players on the same team, they view them as rivals.

A lack of accountability is one of the ways in which rivalry manifests. Let’s use the example of a startup struggling to grow their pipeline. The Sales team may blame marketing by saying they haven’t generated enough high-quality leads. The Marketing team can then turn around and blame Sales, saying they don’t know how to engage leads.

### **3\. Privacy and compliance concerns**

Organizational silos make it difficult for a company to track who is collecting, accessing, and storing sensitive customer data. Without a clear [data governance strategy](https://segment.com/resources/data-strategy/why-a-data-governance-strategy-is-essential-to-your-data-management/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Forganizational-silos), you are more vulnerable to cybersecurity threats, and you risk violating data protection laws.

For instance, GDPR allows [individuals to request that companies delete all of their data](https://segment.com/docs/privacy/user-deletion-and-suppression/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Forganizational-silos). But this is much harder to do if you don’t know all the applications where you have their data stored.

Nowadays, customers are more aware of data privacy issues, making it all the more important to have a good [customer data management](https://segment.com/resources/cdp/customer-data-management/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Forganizational-silos) process in place. When you store data across disparate Excel sheets and apps, the risk of mishandling data increases, opening your organization to backlash and reputational damage.

### **4\. A decline in customer satisfaction**

A siloed organization will inevitably spill over in the customer experience. As we mentioned above, there can be gaps in knowledge regarding the customer journey between departments, leading to a disjointed end-user experience. This can lead to reputational damage, and higher [churn rates](https://segment.com/growth-center/customer-retention/rate/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Forganizational-silos) for the business.

## [How to recognize organizational silos](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos\#how-to-recognize-organizational-silos)

The following are examples of the ill-effects of a siloed organization:

- **Lack of bottom-up communication.** The leadership team is unaware of the challenges faced by employees at the lower levels.

- **Lack of communication between management.** One department head is unaware of important projects other departments are working on.

- **Lack of collaboration and information-sharing between departments.** Teams might even avoid sharing information or have no easy way to do so.

- **Using separate applications to collect data.** For example, customer success may log support tickets in an application developers don’t have access to, leading to siloed information.

- **Task duplication.** Different teams working on the same projects, creating inefficient operations.


## [How to fix organizational silos](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/organizational-silos\#how-to-fix-organizational-silos)

Removing organizational silos requires a multi-pronged approach that tackles team dynamics and data governance.

### **1\. Implement a data governance strategy**

A [data governance strategy](https://segment.com/resources/data-strategy/why-a-data-governance-strategy-is-essential-to-your-data-management/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Forganizational-silos) is a set of guidelines that manage the collection, usage, access, storage, and removal of data. It breaks down organizational silos by implementing a single approach to data governance instead of allowing each silo to develop their own approach to data.

[Segment Protocols](https://segment.com/product/protocols/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Forganizational-silos) supports better data governance by standardizing data collection and ensuring all information used by different teams is consistent and trustworthy.

With a company-wide framework for data governance, you’ll be able to more easily comply with privacy regulations and protect yourself from cybersecurity threats. It will also eliminate the use of bad data, as every team will follow the same data guidelines.

### **2\. Integrate and centralize data**

Considering the cost of poor-quality data, every company that identifies this issue should prioritize breaking down data silos, a process that’s also known as [data orchestration](https://segment.com/resources/data-strategy/what-is-data-orchestration/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Forganizational-silos).

The process consists of three steps:

- Capturing and organizing data from every storage tool or system

- Converting the data into a single format

- Activating the data by making it accessible to data analysis tools


With data silos out of the way, you’re able to implement a [customer data platform (CDP)](https://segment.com/resources/cdp/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Forganizational-silos) to set up a centralized database of your first-party customer data. A CDP will help all teams access and use the same information, allow the democratization of data, and personalize your customer interactions.

A CDP is more advanced compared to a customer relationship management tool (CRM), with some solutions having the ability to sync 30x more data than a CRM. It also provides a single customer view that contains all the data your business has collected on one account from different channels.

### **3\. Encourage cross-departmental collaboration**

Greater cross-departmental collaboration will break down silos, remove any animosity between teams, and help avoid last-minute surprises when launching new products.

While updating an existing product, for instance, developers can refer to the support team to understand the most common issues that customers face. The marketing team can also better understand their audience’s pain points by listening to sales calls.

### **4\. Use team-building exercises**

If organizational silos are deeply entrenched, team-building exercises are necessary to improve the relationships between teams.

A team-building exercise can help employees understand each other’s communication styles and behavior in group projects – knowledge that they can apply when working together.

## Frequently asked questions

### What causes operational silos in an organization?

An icon of a plus symbolAn icon of a minus symbol

Operational silos in an organization can occur when there’s a lack of cross-communication between departments, and a lack of data democratization within an organization.

### Why are company silos bad?

An icon of a plus symbolAn icon of a minus symbol

Company silos are detrimental because the lack of collaboration leads to inefficiencies and slow growth. Organizational silos also lead to data silos, which puts companies at risk of skewed analysis, and potentially even security threats or regulatory violations.

### How can an organization break down organizational silos?

An icon of a plus symbolAn icon of a minus symbol

To break down organizational silos, an organization can implement a data governance strategy, integrate customer data from across teams and tools, and encourage cross-functional collaboration.

### What is the silo effect?

An icon of a plus symbolAn icon of a minus symbol

The silo effect refers to a drop in employee productivity due to organizational silos that stifle collaboration between different departments.

## What Is Return-Path Header (And Why It Matters) | Twilio

> **Source:** https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-return-path

# What Is Return-Path Header (And Why It Matters)

Time to read: 3 minutes

- [Facebook logo](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-return-path "Share via Facebook")

May 15, 2023

**Written by**

[Jesse Sumrak](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/authors/author.jsumrak)

Twilion


* * *

[What Is Return-Path Header (And Why It Matters)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-return-path#introduction)

We can all agree that email communication is essential for successful businesses. However, for your [emails](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/products/email-api) to be successful and produce conversions, they have to land in the inbox.

But what happens when emails _don’t_ make it to the inbox? Where do they go when they bounce? How are they processed?

> Enter return-path email headers.

## [What is return path email header?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-return-path\#what-is-return-path-email-header)

Return-path is a hidden email header that indicates where and how bounced emails will be processed. This header, also referred to as a bounce address or reverse path, is an [SMTP address](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/products/email-api/smtp-service) that is separate from your original sending address, and is used specifically for collecting and processing bounced messages.

Having a clear return-path system in place is incredibly important for your email program. It acts as a safeguard, protecting senders by providing a separate location for processing bounced emails. Your original sending inbox isn’t crowded by those “failed delivery” emails and that bounced messages are kept organized and together. Having a clear, organized return-path for bounced messages can also help your email deliverability and maintain your sending reputation.

## [Why is return-path important?](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-return-path\#span-stylefontweight-400why-is-returnpath-importantspan)

Return-path is an important tool to have at your disposal, especially for [mass email sendsAn icon of a outbound link arrow](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/what-is-an-email-blast.html?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fwhat-is-return-path). Let’s say you’re sending an email blast about an offer your company is promoting to your entire email list. While we don’t want to see bounced emails, the reality is that messages can and do bounce for a variety of reasons.

When you’re sending to large groups, you can get tens, maybe even hundreds of bounced messages depending on the size and nature of your campaign. These “failed delivery” messages then come back to haunt and crowd your original sending inbox. Instead, by having an established return-path, those messages are processed and stored separately in their own specified inbox.

Return-path also helps with your deliverability and sending reputation by helping to validate your identity as a sender (i.e. whether or not you’re sending spam). Because return-path is a SMTP address, it can be used by servers and inbox providers to decide how or if they want to filter your messages. Having a properly set-up return-path can help provide credibility for your messages and subsequently you, the sender, which in turn boosts your sending reputation.

## [How return-path works](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-return-path\#span-stylefontweight-400how-returnpath-worksspan)

Return-path works by directing where bounced messages should go when they cannot be delivered. It is usually set up by a developer or email platform provider but can be customized using the [Domain Authentication docAn icon of a outbound link arrow](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/how-to-set-up-domain-authentication/#using-a-custom-return-path?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fwhat-is-return-path) in our [Knowledge CenterAn icon of a outbound link arrow](https://sendgrid.com/docs/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fwhat-is-return-path).

When a server or inbox provider receives your message, they validate your identity as a sender as well as your sending reputation before pushing you through to your intended recipients’ inboxes.

In this validation process, [DMARCAn icon of a outbound link arrow](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-dmarc) and return-path work together to get you through these filters. DMARC examines your message to confirm that the domain provided in the “sent from” field matches the domain provided in the return-path field, which helps to validate your identity as a sender. Once these domains have been confirmed and matched by DMARC, you’ll have an easier time getting through filters set by servers and inbox providers.

### [Types of bounced emails](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-return-path\#types-of-bounced-emails)

There are two types of bounced emails: [hard bounces and soft bouncesAn icon of a outbound link arrow](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/email-bounce-management.html?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fwhat-is-return-path).

**Hard bounces** occur when there are permanent issues with a recipient, including an invalid email address or typo in your mailing list.

**Soft bounces** are more temporary and usually occur when there’s a problem with a recipient’s inbox, including file size or attachments issues or the possibility of a recipient having a full inbox.

When a message hard bounces, the general best practice is to check that there are no typos in the recipient’s address. If there are none, you should remove the address from your mailing list. Keeping email addresses that hard bounce can damage your reputation as a sender and affect your deliverability in the long run.

When an email soft bounces, you have a little bit more wiggle room than with a hard bounce. Email addresses that soft bounce can be kept in your mailing list for future campaigns, but you’ll want to watch them to see if they bounce again. If they continue to bounce, they should be removed from your mailing list.

## [How to customize your return-path in SendGrid](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-return-path\#span-stylefontweight-400how-to-customize-your-returnpath-in-sendgridspan)

Twilio SendGrid sets up an automatic return-path for our customers. This helps us protect both you and your customers, as well as give your deliverability a boost! However, your return-path can be [customized during the domain authentication processAn icon of a outbound link arrow](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/how-to-set-up-domain-authentication/#using-a-custom-return-path?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fwhat-is-return-path).

When you are in the process of authenticating a domain, open the advanced settings found on the same screen used to input the domain settings. From there, you’ll be able to build a custom return-path. However, for this process to work, you must use different characters from the ones that Twilio SendGrid automatically assigned to you.

Having a clear, systematic return-path is essential to creating a successful email program and improving your deliverability. For best practice tips on improving deliverability and developing strong email communication strategies, check out [our blogAn icon of a outbound link arrow](https://sendgrid.com/blog/?utm_referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.twilio.com%2Fen-us%2Fblog%2Finsights%2Fwhat-is-return-path).
